notes.meaning: Jesus finished His long teaching about the future and the end of the world. Now He turned His attention toward His coming death. He was ready to give His life willingly to save His people.

Jesus reminded His followers that the Passover feast was only two days away. Passover was the Jewish holy day celebrating how God rescued Israel from slavery in Egypt. Jesus announced that He would be handed over and nailed to a cross as the true Passover sacrifice.

The Jewish religious leaders met secretly at the palace of the high priest named Caiaphas. This group made up the Sanhedrin, the highest Jewish ruling council. Because they hated Jesus, they gathered in private to find a way to get rid of Him.

The leaders plotted to capture Jesus by trickery and put Him to death. They knew He had many followers, so they did not dare to arrest Him openly in public. They wanted a quiet plan so the crowds would not stop them.

The leaders agreed not to arrest Jesus during the week-long festival. Huge crowds filled Jerusalem for the feast, and the leaders feared a riot if the people defended Him. Yet God overruled their human plans so that Jesus would die on the exact day of Passover.

Jesus attended a dinner in Bethany at the house of a man called Simon the Leper. Simon had likely been cured of leprosy by Jesus, since a person with active skin disease was not allowed to host guests. Jesus gladly spent time with people who had once been cast out of society.

While Jesus was eating, a woman approached Him with an expensive jar of perfumed oil. She poured this sweet-smelling oil over His head to show deep love and honour. The perfume was worth nearly a whole year of a worker's wages.

The disciples grew angry when they saw the oil poured out. They called this loving act a total waste of money. Led by Judas, they failed to understand why such an expensive gift was given directly to Jesus.

The disciples complained that the perfume could have been sold for a huge sum to help the poor. On the surface, this sounded kind and generous. In truth, some used care for the poor as an excuse to mask greed and complain.

Jesus stepped in to defend the woman from their harsh words. He told the disciples to stop upsetting her because she had done a noble and beautiful deed for Him. Jesus gladly receives what we give Him out of sincere love.

Jesus explained that they would always have poor people near them who needed help. Caring for the poor is an ongoing duty, but His earthly presence with them was almost at an end. This was a special, unrepeatable moment to honour Him in person before His death.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Christ is not always present in a visible, earthly manner, but he remains truly present with the church in the mystery of the Eucharist.

notes.meaning: In Jewish custom, bodies were anointed with sweet oils and spices before being placed in a tomb. Jesus explained that the woman had actually prepared His body for burial. Even if she did not fully understand what was coming, her act pointed straight to His near death.

Jesus promised that wherever the good news of salvation was preached across the world, this woman's act would be remembered. Great rulers and earthly kingdoms fade away, but her humble deed of love has never been forgotten. Her story shows that Jesus values every sacrifice made for Him.

Right after this dinner, Judas Iscariot went to the chief priests. Although he was one of Jesus's closest twelve followers, he allowed greed and resentment to control his heart. He decided to turn against his own Master.

Judas asked the priests how much money they would give him to hand Jesus over. They counted out thirty silver coins, which was the legal price of an ordinary slave. The leaders treated the Lord of glory as though He were worth almost nothing.

Once the bargain was made, Judas looked for the right moment to hand Jesus over. He needed a time when Jesus was away from the crowds so there would not be an uproar. Sin had taken hold of his heart, and he pursued his wicked plan with determination.

On the day when the Passover lamb was to be sacrificed, the disciples asked Jesus where they should prepare the meal. During this feast, Jewish families ate unleavened bread, which was flat bread made without yeast to remember their quick escape from Egypt. The disciples wanted to make sure they followed God's law properly.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars note a difficulty between the Gospels, suggesting Jesus may have held His meal one evening early because He knew He would be killed before the official feast.

notes.meaning: Jesus sent them into Jerusalem to a specific homeowner to request a room. He told them to say that His appointed time of suffering and death had arrived. Jesus knew in advance who would welcome Him and where the meal would take place.

The disciples obeyed Jesus and prepared everything required for the Passover. This meant having the lamb sacrificed at the temple, roasting the meat, and setting out the bitter herbs, wine, and flat bread. Their ready obedience showed their trust in Jesus's word.

When night fell, Jesus reclined at the table with the twelve apostles. In Bible times, guests leaned on cushions around a low table for important feasts rather than sitting on chairs. This was a warm, close gathering of Jesus and His inner circle.

In the middle of the sacred meal, Jesus announced that one of them would betray Him. To betray someone means to hand over a friend to their enemies by breaking trust. This statement shocked the disciples and caused deep distress around the table.

The disciples were filled with deep sorrow and began asking, one after another, if they were the traitor. Instead of pointing fingers at each other, each disciple searched his own heart with honesty and humility. Their question showed that they loved Jesus and dreaded turning away from Him.

Jesus answered that His betrayer was someone dipping bread into the common bowl with Him. In that culture, sharing a meal was a sacred bond of friendship and loyalty. Betraying someone while sharing food with them made the crime even more terrible.

Jesus stated that He would die just as the Old Testament prophets had foretold. Even though God used this event in His divine plan, the man who handed Him over was still fully guilty of his sin. Judas's punishment would be so terrible that it would have been better for him never to have been born.

Judas finally spoke up and asked if he was the one, calling Jesus 'Rabbi' or Teacher instead of 'Lord.' Jesus quietly answered that Judas had said it himself, confirming that He knew the plot. Even when his secret guilt was uncovered, Judas refused to turn back from his betrayal.
